resources.string: Marker emptied: %1$s%% of the starting amount

Let f be the selected removal percentage divided by 100. Each interval removes f times the marker then present, leaving a fraction (1 − f). After n intervals, the percent of the starting marker remaining is 100 × (1 − f)^n. Percent emptied is 100 minus percent remaining.

The stomach releases liquid contents through the pylorus into the duodenum. Real emptying is regulated and can vary with the energy density of the liquid. This model tracks a fictional marker in one perfectly mixed compartment. No marker is added, absorbed, or broken down; it only leaves with the outflow. The removal percentage is invented, and intervals have no physical duration. For teaching only: this does not predict digestion or personal gastric emptying and is not for clinical use.
